title: Parametrized finite and complete scalar cocycle averaging primitives
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a nonarchimedean normed field $V$ containing $\mathbf Q_\ell$ isometrically [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let $G$ be a profinite group, meaning a compact Hausdorff topological group with a basis of open normal subgroups, every finite continuous quotient of which has order prime to $\ell$. Let $P$ be a profinite space, meaning a compact Hausdorff space with a clopen basis. All spaces use [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $C^r(P,G;V)=C(P\times G^r,V)$ for all continuous maps, with trivial group action, $d^0=0$, and for $r\geq1$
$$(dc)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=c(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{a=1}^r(-1)^a c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_r).$$
For every $n\geq1$, if a cocycle $c\in C^n(P,G;V)$ factors in the group coordinates through $Q=G/U$ for an open normal $U$, its descended cochain $\bar c$ has the primitive
$$b(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1})={(-1)^n\over |Q|}\sum_{h\in Q}\bar c(s;\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_{n-1},h).$$
This is a continuous cochain factoring through the same quotient, with $db=c$ and $\|b\|_\infty\leq\|c\|_\infty$. No completeness of $V$ is required in this assertion.
If $V$ is complete, let $I_G:C(G,V)\to V$ be the normalized translation-invariant $V$-linear integral with supremum-norm bound one of [lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-complete-scalar-integral] (for $B=V$ and $K=G$). Then the $V$-linear maps $h_{V,G}^n:C^n(*,G;V)\to C^{n-1}(*,G;V)$ given by
$$(h_{V,G}^n c)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1})=(-1)^n I_G(h\mapsto c(g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1},h))$$
are contractions. For every profinite $P$, applying $h_{V,G}^n$ fibrewise sends continuous $P$-families to continuous $P$-families, is $C(P,V)$-linear, commutes with continuous changes of parameter, and has supremum-norm bound one. For every cocycle $c$ in such a family, $d h_{V,G}^n c=c$. These conclusions include $n=1$, where the cocycle is zero, and the empty $P$, where all cochains are zero.

proof.text: Use lem-sfb-finite-quotient-contractive-average, installing the normed Padic algebra structure from the specified isometric embedding. Form the signed finite sum of last-variable quotient restrictions as a continuous map bbar; pull it back to b. The factorization hypothesis places every last-variable slice in the averaging submodule D. Its finite-sum formula identifies b pointwise with the signed average. Apply lem-sfb-invariant-average-cochain-identity to E=D, pointwise evaluation, and the stated normalized invariant average. Its contraction bound followed by the continuous-map supremum-norm estimate gives the norm bound, including empty P.

For the supplied continuous linear functional I, curry the cochain after the continuous map ((s,g),h) to (s,snoc g h), compose with I and multiply by the sign. This constructs H explicitly as a linear map of continuous-map spaces, without choosing any witness from an existence theorem. Evaluation gives the stated slice formula, C(P,V)-linearity and naturality. Contractivity of I and the pointwise supremum estimate give the norm bound.

Apply lem-sfb-invariant-average-cochain-identity with E=C(G,V), faithful pointwise evaluation, A=I and oneE=1. Left translations are continuous and preserve the integral by its supplied hypothesis. The result is exactly the primitive identity. The general algebraic calculation includes n=0 and the continuous-map norm inequalities require no nonemptiness of P.
